newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end firm after mixed session.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end firm after mixed session.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended slightly firmer on Thursday, after a mixed session with selective interest in blue chip issues, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed up 32.60 points at 11,636.13. Turnover was HK$4.54 billion compared to HK$5.43 billion on Wednesday.
"The market today has been very mixed," said Robin Hammond, Hong Kong research director Asia Equity.
"There's moderate volume but no particular pattern in the market. We have had a damn good run and there is no particular reason to rush in at this point," he said.
Hang Seng September futures, which expire on Friday, ended the session 38 points higher at 11,618.
Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities, said the Hang Seng index may remain around current levels until Sun Hung Kai Properties announces its final results on Wednesday next week.
"I don't see much momentum at all. The trading range was very narrow today," he said.
The Hang Seng index hit a session high of 11,668.70 and a low of 11,594.58.

"The market is not likely to break out of this range for the moment except if Sun Hung Kai Properties results are better than expected. If the market hangs around this level even after Sun Hung Kai's results, then it will definitely have a correction of 200 to 300 points," Chan added.
Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$0.50 to HK$79.75. Other property stocks were also firm with Cheung Kong up HK$0.25 at HK$57.00 and Henderson Land up HK$0.25 at HK$64.50.
Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities, said much of Thursday's activity was concentrated on second liner stocks. "For blue chips it was pretty quiet," he said.
On the actives list, CNPC (Hong Kong) rose HK$0.03 to HK$0.55 and Chung Hwa Development rose HK$0.11 to HK$1.40.

Kwoon Chung Bus Holdings Ltd succumbed to profit-taking on its second day of trading, ending down HK$0.225 at HK$2.125. Shares of the bus operator rose HK$0.55 on Wednesday from their issue price to end at HK$2.35.
HSBC Holdings rose HK$1.00 to HK$142.00 but Hang Seng Bank fell HK$0.25 to HK$79.25.
Shares in Peregrine Investments rose HK$0.30 to HK$11.90 after the company reported a 15 percent rise in interim net profit to HK$399 million. -- J.Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
